propositions: _recall_false_accept computes specificity (true-negative rate, higher-is-better) but treats it as an error rate (lower-is-better) at comparison sites, inverting the gate logic

the false-accept ceiling at max_false_accept=0.10 is effectively always-fail because competent gates have specificity far above 0.10, while the corrected false-positive rate would be meaningfully constrained

the frontier slot of the live Bedrock parity run failed on false-accept rising 0.143pp (v1 0.786 to v2 0.929) when Bedrock actually made fewer false-positive blocks than Anthropic (0.071 vs 0.214), demonstrating the metric penalizes accuracy improvements

correcting the computation to return blocked/safe (false-positive rate) rather than not-blocked/safe leaves existing comparison directions unchanged and aligns parity with the settled false_accept definition in eval.py and release gate docs
fidelity_spot_eval.py had encoded the inverted metric by labelling must-block conflicts as advisory (safe), surviving only while false_accept wrongly counted not-blocked items
